$comment: Shared, committed Claude Code config so every checkout gets the same safety posture and pre-approved permissions. Machine-specific overrides go in the gitignored .claude/settings.local.json. deny takes precedence over allow, so these blocks hold even under --dangerously-skip-permissions (used by ops/gentriduck-devmode.sh on the native Linux automation host). The 'git push ... main' deny rules are DEFENCE-IN-DEPTH only (ADR-0011): they match 'main' as a ref token (not the substring, so 'domain'/'maintenance' branch names are safe), but exotic forms like 'git push origin HEAD' on a checked-out main, or '--mirror', are NOT caught. main's real protection is the denied gh pr merge + the PM being instructed to only ever touch develop; full enforcement needs a separate PM identity (ADR-0011 Alternative D) or a server-side ruleset (SEC-1, #190, blocked on maintainer repo-settings action). SEC-2 (#191): the allow-list used to include a blanket 'Bash(gh *)', which let 'gh api repos/.../pulls/N/merge -X PUT' bypass the 'gh pr merge' deny, and 'gh api .../git/refs/heads/main -X PATCH' bypass the push-to-main denies (deny patterns match the Bash command string, not what it executes) -- 'gh api' is now dropped from the allow-list entirely (no committed script needs it; falls back to a permission prompt if ever required). Accepted residual risk (SEC-2): deny/allow patterns match the literal command string, so 'python3 -c "...gh api..."' or 'xargs gh api' indirection can still slip past both the gh-subcommand allow-list and the deny-list -- this is why SEC-1's server-side ruleset on main/develop is the real backstop, not this file. 'rm *'/'curl *'/'wget *' stay broadly allowed because the ingestion pipeline (ingestion/*.py) legitimately downloads and cleans up scratch files; scoping those tighter is out of SEC-2's scope.
